app.name: MathTiba
app.tagline: We find the misconception, not the score.

home.lead: MathTiba identifies the misconception beneath a student's failure, traces it to the prerequisite gap that caused it, and measures whether it is actually gone.
home.footer: Misconceptions derived from NECTA CIRA reports 2018–2024 · Prerequisite graph from TIE syllabus 2023
home.howLead: A different kind of assessment, built on a national exam problem that has repeated for seven consecutive years.
home.howStep1Body: 22 adaptive items. Every wrong answer is not random — each distractor is mapped to one of eight documented misconceptions from NECTA's own exam analysis.
home.howStep2Body: MathTiba walks a prerequisite graph, not a curriculum list. A Form 2 student failing linear equations is often failing Form 1 fractions instead.
home.howStep3Body: The student practises with a structured ACTION + REASON workspace, then is re-tested with a different surface but the same underlying misconception.
home.aboutBody: In CSEE 2024, 74.65% of candidates failed Basic Mathematics — a pattern that has held for seven years, and the 2025 results (released January 2026) show 73.55% still failing. MathTiba does not claim to fix Tanzanian mathematics education. It claims something smaller and provable: it can change what a failure means, from a single number to a traceable, evidence-linked misconception with a targeted intervention.
home.aboutPrinciple: AI never performs mathematics. All numerical verification is deterministic (exact rational arithmetic, mirrored in SymPy). A separate, optional generative layer may phrase an already-computed diagnostic summary in plain language — it is never asked to verify or compute anything.
home.aboutResearchTitle: Grounded in existing research, not invented from scratch
home.aboutResearchBody: The idea that student errors follow consistent, diagnosable rules rather than random noise goes back to Payne & Squibb's 1990 "mal-rules" theory of algebra errors (Cognitive Science, 14(3)). Recent work applying large language models to this same problem (e.g. GPT-4 on middle-school algebra misconceptions) reports around 84% detection accuracy on ambiguous cases. MathTiba deliberately avoids asking a language model to infer a misconception from free text: every misconception is observed directly from a pre-designed distractor a student chose, which is why the engineering validation harness reaches 96% recovery with 0% false positives within its scoped domain — a narrower claim than "AI can detect any misconception", and a more defensible one.

reasons.R_BALANCE: Because both sides of an equation must stay equal
reasons.R_ISOLATE: Because we want the variable on its own
reasons.R_MOVE_ACROSS: Because the term moves to the other side
reasons.R_LIKE_TERMS: Because only like terms can be combined
reasons.R_SIMPLER: Because it makes the expression shorter
reasons.R_SAME_LETTER: Because the terms share the same letter
reasons.R_DISTRIBUTE_ALL: Because the multiplier applies to every term inside
reasons.R_REMOVE_BRACKET: Because the brackets need to go
reasons.R_FIRST_TERM: Because the multiplier applies to the first term

arithmeticReasons.R_COMMON_DENOM: Because a common denominator makes the parts comparable
arithmeticReasons.R_STRAIGHT_ACROSS: Because you add the tops and add the bottoms
arithmeticReasons.R_OF_REMAINDER: Because each percentage applies to the current amount, not the original
arithmeticReasons.R_ADD_PERCENTS: Because percentages can just be added directly
arithmeticReasons.R_MULTIPLES: Because LCM is the smallest shared multiple of both numbers
arithmeticReasons.R_CONFUSE_GCF: Because I found the largest shared factor instead
arithmeticReasons.R_MEMORIZED: Because that's the rule I memorized

arithmetic.incorrect: Not quite — check the calculation and try again.

topicDescriptions.NUM-OPS: LCM, GCF, integers and foundational number skills.
topicDescriptions.SETS: Set notation, union, intersection and Venn diagrams.
topicDescriptions.FRACTIONS: Equivalent fractions, comparison and the four operations.
topicDescriptions.INDICES: Laws of indices and exponent rules.
topicDescriptions.MENSURATION: Area, perimeter, surface area and volume formulas.
topicDescriptions.RATIO: Comparing quantities and solving proportional problems.
topicDescriptions.PERCENTAGES: Percent of a quantity, increase, decrease and money problems.
topicDescriptions.SURDS: Simplifying and operating on irrational roots.
topicDescriptions.LOGARITHMS: Logarithm laws and solving log equations.
topicDescriptions.PROBABILITY: Simple and combined events, tree diagrams.
topicDescriptions.BUSINESS-MATH: Commission, hire purchase, compound interest and cash accounts.
topicDescriptions.VARIATION: Direct, inverse and joint variation problems.
topicDescriptions.STATISTICS: Mean, median, mode, frequency tables and histograms.
topicDescriptions.TRIGONOMETRY: Sine, cosine, tangent and the sine/cosine rules.
topicDescriptions.SEQUENCES: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.
topicDescriptions.LIN-EQ: Solve equations and show every valid balancing step.
topicDescriptions.EARTH-GEOM: Longitude, latitude and distance on the Earth's surface.
topicDescriptions.COORD-GEOM: Gradient, distance, midpoint and equations of a line.
topicDescriptions.SIMUL-EQ: Solving two equations in two unknowns.
topicDescriptions.QUADRATIC-EQ: Factoring, the quadratic formula and completing the square.
topicDescriptions.LINEAR-PROG: Graphing constraints and optimizing an objective function.
topicDescriptions.GEOMETRY: Angles, polygons, circles and geometric reasoning.
